findings.title: Recurring calendar deletes are no longer awaited
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining occurrences, calendar credentials are still walked with forEach(async ...). getCalendar is now awaited inside that callback, and deleteEvent is only pushed onto apiDeletes after that await. forEach does not wait for async callbacks, so execution continues and later Promise.all(apiDeletes) often runs before those pushes happen. Recurring Google/Outlook/etc. events can therefore be left on the calendar while the handler still returns success, and a rejection from getCalendar becomes an unhandled rejection instead of failing the request. Collect the credentials with a for...of (as the non-recurring branch just below does) and push each deleteEvent promise before awaiting them.

findings.title: Reschedule calendar cleanup is fire-and-forget
findings.body: requestReschedule marks the booking cancelled and then calls bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach ignores the returned promises, and the mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks without waiting. Because getCalendar is now async, the external delete is not even started until after the import resolves, so a serverless handler can finish and freeze before the calendar or video event is removed. Errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent are also unhandled. Await Promise.all over the references (or a for...of) before sending email and webhooks.

findings.title: Vital reschedule try/catch no longer covers calendar deletes
findings.body: The try block uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) and awaits getCalendar inside the callback. forEach does not await that callback, so the surrounding try/catch cannot see rejections from the new async getCalendar (or from deleteEvent). The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true while calendar/video deletion may still be pending or may have failed. Replace forEach with an awaited Promise.all/for...of so failures are logged and deletes finish before the email is sent. The same pattern is in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts at the matching forEach.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise as calendar
findings.body: getCalendarCredentials stays synchronous but stores the result of the now-async getCalendar without awaiting it. The exported calendar field is therefore Promise<Calendar | null>, which is always truthy, rather than Calendar | null. getConnectedCalendars in this file awaits item.calendar, but any other caller that treats calendar as a Calendar instance (calling listCalendars/createEvent, or checking null) will either skip a missing integration incorrectly or throw at runtime. The return type should be updated and every caller should await the promise, or this helper should become async and resolve calendars before returning.
